$comment: Vanilla API tables of components without a create<Name> controller. Step 30 compares such a table with the union of the classes and data-*/aria-* attributes that the '## Stable class and state API' table of the @hawiyah/styles README documents for the component's classes (components.json cssClasses) and the attribute selectors that the installed dist/styles.css has on those classes, plus a row 'class'. A row that neither declares is allowed only through this file: nativeAttributes are attributes defined by HTML or ARIA that the page lists (their name and kind are compared; Type, Required and Default are not, because no published file declares them), notListed are documented or selected attributes the page leaves out. The list is the lead's: every entry carries approvedBy and a reason, and every attribute a reason; writers propose entries in their result files.

vanilla.reason: Button is a native button element styled by the class hw-button, and @hawiyah/vanilla 0.3.0 exports no createButton (its only export with Button in the name is createCopyButton, the controller of the copy button). The Actions row of '## Stable class and state API' in the @hawiyah/styles 0.3.0 README documents hw-button, data-variant, data-size and data-icon-only, and dist/styles.css selects aria-busy, aria-disabled, aria-pressed, data-shape and disabled on .hw-button; step 30 reads both.

nativeAttributes.type: HTML attribute of the button element, not a Hawiyah declaration; the page lists it because the browser default of a button in a form is submit.

vanilla.review: Checked against the stylesheet contract and again against the attribute selectors of the stylesheet: aria-busy and disabled are no longer entries, because dist/styles.css of @hawiyah/styles 0.3.0 selects them in a compound with .hw-button and step 30 now reads the stylesheet's attribute selectors. type is defined by HTML and no selector of the stylesheet names it on .hw-button.
